nodes_add.name: Sister Nivedita (Margaret Noble)
nodes_add.note: Irish disciple of Vivekananda, initiated as a brahmacharini on 25 March 1898; author of The Master as I Saw Him (1910).

nodes_update.name: Swami Vivekananda
nodes_update.note: Narendranath Datta. Ramakrishna's chief disciple; 1893 Parliament of Religions; four yogas and Practical Vedanta; founded the Ramakrishna Mission (1 May 1897).

edges_upsert.note: Guru and disciple from late 1881/early 1882 until Ramakrishna's death in August 1886; nursed him at Cossipore. Formal sannyasa vows taken by the disciples themselves in early 1887.
Shankara's Advaita, reinterpreted as Practical Vedanta.
Attended Keshab's Nava Vidhan c. 1880 and his Band of Hope 1881-1884; later joined the Sadharan Brahmo Samaj.
Brahmacharya initiation and the name Nivedita, 25 March 1898, Calcutta.
Aurobindo wrote (1934) that in Alipore jail Vivekananda 'was speaking with me for about 15 days' as a presence in meditation; also read his works.
Rama Tirtha met Vivekananda in Lahore in 1897 and later credited the meeting as an inspiration for his renunciation (1899); sourced to Wikipedia only, Rama Tirtha writer to confirm.
Ramakrishna Order; Vedanta Society of New York, founded by Vivekananda in 1894.

places.name: Vivekananda's birthplace, 3 Gourmohan Mukherjee Street (now 105 Vivekananda Road), Calcutta
places.what: Birthplace (1863); now the Ramakrishna Mission Swami Vivekananda's Ancestral House and Cultural Centre (opened 2004)

places.name: Thousand Island Park, New York
places.what: Summer classes, about seven weeks in 1895 (Inspired Talks); Vivekananda Cottage

places.name: Khetri, Rajasthan
places.what: Court of his patron Raja Ajit Singh (visits 1891 and 1893), who by most accounts suggested the name Vivekananda

glossary.def: Vivekananda's name for Advaita applied to everyday life: since the one Self is in everyone, serving others, especially the poor, is worship.
The path of work done without attachment to its results, one of Vivekananda's four yogas.
The path of meditation and mental control based on Patanjali's Yoga Sutras; also the title of Vivekananda's 1896 book.
Pronounced 'mutt'. A Hindu monastery; the Ramakrishna Math is the monastic order founded by Vivekananda.
A wandering monk with no fixed home.

issues: vivekananda.mdx: the Dakshineswar episode in which Ramakrishna corrects 'compassion for jivas' to service of beings as God is sourced here only to a Ramakrishna Mission Delhi article; it is traditionally from Saradananda's Lilaprasanga (Sri Ramakrishna, the Great Master). Fact-checker should confirm the chapter, and coordinate wording with the Ramakrishna chapter.

vivekananda.mdx: 'Within months of its founding, the Mission's monks were running famine relief in rural Bengal' (Akhandananda, Murshidabad, 1897) is from general knowledge, not fetched. Verify or cut.
vivekananda.mdx: Kanyakumari 'swam or was rowed out' is hedged; Order accounts say he swam. Date given as late December 1892 (Wikipedia: arrived 24 Dec, meditated 25-27 Dec).
vivekananda.mdx: biographies' claim of diabetes and asthma, the Kayastha caste, and the Spencer translation are from Wikipedia without a second source.

vivekananda.mdx: 'The Ideal of a Universal Religion' is named without a date or place; the claim that he ranked dualism, qualified non-dualism and Advaita as stages is standard but not quoted from a fetched text.
vivekananda.mdx: no voice recording survives (Belur Math, 2020). Photographs from Chicago 1893 exist but no openly licensed image URL was checked, so no photo block.
Edge vivekananda -> rama-tirtha left verified:false; the Rama Tirtha writer should confirm.
Coordinates for birthplace, Thousand Island Park and Khetri are approximate (two decimals) and marked verified:false.

Overlap with the Ramakrishna chapter: the first meeting ('have you seen God'), the Kali episode after his father's death and the service episode are summarised briefly here; the Ramakrishna writer may tell them in full. Check the two chapters agree on the first-meeting date (Nov 1881 at Surendranath Mitra's house; Dakshineswar late 1881 or early 1882).

Factcheck: please cite the Great Master/Divine Play chapter for the 'serve beings as Shiva' episode from a print copy, and confirm the Kayastha/Spencer details in the Life by His Eastern and Western Disciples.

vivekananda: Born Narendranath Datta 12 Jan 1863, 3 Gourmohan Mukherjee St; father attorney Calcutta High Court; mother Bhubaneswari Devi; Metropolitan Institution 1871; Raipur 1877; BA 1884 General Assembly's Institution -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swami_Vivekananda
Nava Vidhan 1880, Sadharan Brahmo Samaj, Band of Hope 1881-84; asked Debendranath Tagore if he had seen God -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swami_Vivekananda
First meeting with Ramakrishna probably Nov 1881 at Surendra Nath Mitra's house; Dakshineswar late 1881 or early 1882 -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swami_Vivekananda
Father died 1884; Ramakrishna died 16 Aug 1886 at Cossipore; Baranagar math; Christmas Eve 1886 Antpur with eight others -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swami_Vivekananda
Wandering from 1888; Ajit Singh of Khetri suggested the name Vivekananda -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swami_Vivekananda
Kanyakumari, arrived 24 Dec 1892, meditated 25-27 Dec; letter to Ramakrishnananda 19 Mar 1894 'on the last bit of Indian rock' -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanyakumari_resolve_of_1892

Sailed Bombay 31 May 1893; Chicago 30 Jul 1893; Parliament 11-27 Sep 1893; two-minute ovation -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swami_Vivekananda ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swami_Vivekananda_at_the_Parliament_of_the_World%27s_Religions
John Henry Wright of Harvard; 'like asking the sun to state its right to shine' (paraphrased) -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swami_Vivekananda_at_the_Parliament_of_the_World%27s_Religions

Quotes 'We believe not only in universal toleration, but we accept all religions as true.' and 'As the different streams having their sources in different places all mingle their water in the sea' -> https://theprint.in/india/sisters-and-brothers-of-america-full-text-of-swami-vivekanandas-iconic-chicago-speech/257916/ ; https://vivekananda.net/BooksBySwami/CompleteWorks/1_Response.html
20 Sep 1893 'It is an insult to a starving people to offer them religion'; missionaries/souls/bodies -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Religion_not_the_crying_need_of_India

Vedanta Society of New York 1894; Thousand Island Park from June 1895, about two months, about a dozen disciples; Margaret Noble Nov 1895; Max Muller May 1896 -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swami_Vivekananda
Raja Yoga published 1896; preface 'Each soul is potentially divine. The goal is to manifest this Divinity within by controlling nature, external and internal.' -> https://vedanta.org/?p=3512
Practical Vedanta Part I, London, 10 Nov 1896; 'intensely practical'; 'forest caves to busy streets and cities' -> https://vivekananda.net/BooksBySwami/PracticalVedanta/Part1.html
Left England 16 Dec 1896; Colombo 15 Jan 1897; Ramakrishna Mission founded 1 May 1897 -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swami_Vivekananda
Relics installed at Belur 9 Dec 1898 -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belur_Math
Nivedita: born 28 Oct 1867 Dungannon; initiated 25 Mar 1898; died 13 Oct 1911 Darjeeling; The Master as I Saw Him 1910 -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sister_Nivedita
Second trip West June 1899 - 9 Dec 1900; died 4 Jul 1902 at Belur Math, 9:20 pm, aged 39; reported rupture of blood vessel in brain -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swami_Vivekananda
Motto 'Atmano mokshartham jagad hitaya cha', formulated by Vivekananda -> https://indore.rkmm.org/ramakrishna-order-of-monks
Dakshineswar episode: 'Compassion for the Jivas' corrected to service to God in man; Narendra said he heard something new -> https://media.rkmdelhi.org/?p=4571

No recording of his voice known; recorded a couple of times but untraced; Parliament speeches not recorded (Swami Suvirananda, 11 Sep 2020) -> https://media.belurmath.org/clarification-on-swami-vivekanandas-voice-recording-swami-suvirananda-video-6719/
Viral 'recording' is from the film Vivekananda by Vivekananda (dir. Karthik Saragur) -> https://www.boomlive.in/movie-clipping-shared-as-rare-recording-of-vivekanandas-speech-in-chicago
Rambachan, The Limits of Scripture, University of Hawaii Press 1994: experience vs Shankara's scriptural authority -> https://openlibrary.org/isbn/0824815424

Hacker 1962 'Schopenhauer and Hindu ethics': tat tvam asi ethic via Deussen (met Sept 1896); Killingley reply in Radice ed. -> https://loveofallwisdom.com/2010/08/schopenhauer-and-the-tat-tvam-asi-ethic/

De Michelis, A History of Modern Yoga (2004): Raja Yoga as start of modern yoga; Brahmo/Keshab influence -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_History_of_Modern_Yoga ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swami_Vivekananda
Medhananda, Swami Vivekananda's Vedantic Cosmopolitanism (OUP 2022): rejects both Shankara-follower and Neo-Vedantin readings -> https://philarchive.org/rec/MEDSVV

Sharma, A Restatement of Religion (Yale 2013): Vivekananda and the making of Hindu nationalism -> https://yalebooks.yale.edu/book/9780300197402/restatement-religion ; reply summarised at https://api.philpapers.org/rec/MEDWSV
National Youth Day declared 1984, first observed 1985 -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Youth_Day_(India)

Aurobindo: 'he was speaking with me for about 15 days' (1934 letter), Alipore jail -> https://search.motherandsriaurobindo.in/_StaticContent/SriAurobindoAshram/-09 E-Library/-01 Works of Sri Aurobindo/-01 English/-03_CWSA/-35_Letters On Himself And The Ashram/-25_Experiences in Alipur Jail 1908 ­ 1909.htm

changes: vivekananda.mdx: two-minute ovation attributed to 'Biographies' instead of 'Accounts from the hall'; no contemporary report of the duration found (Smithsonian NMAA blog and Wikipedia give only 'thunderous applause').

vivekananda.mdx: famine relief sentence made specific: Swami Akhandananda opened the first famine relief work at Mahula, Murshidabad, 15 May 1897, weeks after the Mission's founding (belurmath.org/past-presidents/swami-akhandananda). Reference 20 added.

vivekananda.mdx: 'stages' of dualism/qualified non-dualism/Advaita reattributed to 'The Vedanta Philosophy' (Harvard, 1896), which says the interpretations 'have been progressive'; 'The Ideal of a Universal Religion' kept for the philosopher/devotee/mystic/worker point. Reference 21 added.

vivekananda.mdx: Killingley reply: removed the claim that Killingley argued the Dakshineswar episode predates Deussen (not in the source, loveofallwisdom.com); his point restated as the meeting sharpening an existing idea; Dakshineswar point attributed to the Order's tradition.
vivekananda.mdx: Thousand Island Park 'some two months' -> 'some seven weeks' (Wikipedia, Thousand Island Park, NY; Order dates 19 June to early August 1895).
vivekananda.mdx: time of death 'about nine' -> 'about twenty past nine' (9.20 pm per Wikipedia and Order accounts).
vivekananda.mdx: Places list, Khetri year 1893 -> 1891–1893 (visits in 1891 and 1893), fixing chronological order.

w05.json: birthplace coordinates corrected to 22.5863, 88.3674 (ancestral house, now 105 Vivekananda Road; old value 22.59, 88.36 was ~700 m off); Thousand Island Park 44.2883, -76.0258 (historic district); Khetri 28.0035, 75.7885; all marked verified.
w05.json: rama-tirtha edge given year 1897 (Lahore meeting, Wikipedia Rama_Tirtha); still verified:false.
unresolved: Dakshineswar 'Shiva jnane jiva seva' episode: could not locate the chapter in Saradananda's Lilaprasanga / Sri Ramakrishna the Great Master online. Only Order-affiliated secondary accounts found (Shantatmananda, rkmdelhi; kamarpukurjayrambati.com), none citing a chapter. The text already attributes it to 'the Order's tradition'; author should cite Great Master (Divine Play) part/chapter from a print copy. The Ramakrishna chapter does not tell this episode, so no wording conflict.
Kayastha caste and the Bengali translation of Spencer's Education rest on Wikipedia only; no second online source found. Both are standard in the Order's Life, which should be checked in print.
Illnesses: diabetes confirmed by a second source (Shankar, The Monk as Man, via hinduwebsite.com); asthma only in Wikipedia.
Hacker essay date: given as 1962 by loveofallwisdom.com; some bibliographies may give 1961 (Saeculum). Not resolved.
Two-minute ovation: traditional biographical detail; no contemporary newspaper source for the duration found.
'All morning ... he asked to speak later' and 'He had never addressed a large audience' rest on the Order's biography (not independently checked).
